# COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE REPORT
**Feature:** Post-transaction rewards breakdown display  
**Analyst:** Senior CI Analyst, HDFC PIXEL Studio  
**Date:** 2026

---

## COMPETITORS

### 1. OneCard (CSB Bank/IDFC First Bank) | OneCard App [DIGITAL-FIRST]
- **Why relevant:** Mobile-first credit card with real-time in-app transaction statements and instant reward point issuance/redemption
- **What they built:** The OneCard app shows "rewards earned" in transaction analytics section where users can track spend categories and rewards earned per transaction. The app provides real-time transaction statements with immediate reward point crediting visible in-app, allowing users to see exactly what they earned on each purchase.
- **One key point:** Users can track rewards earned alongside transaction details in the analytics dashboard, though the source doesn't specify if this appears immediately post-transaction or only in history view.
- **Confidence:** High (has URL)
- **Source:** https://www.csb.bank.in/pdf/CC-FAQ21122022.pdf

### 2. Scapia (Federal Bank) | Scapia Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
- **Why relevant:** Travel-focused credit card with zero forex markup and digital-first experience targeting transparency in rewards
- **What they built:** Not found in current sources - sources mention the card's zero-fee structure and travel benefits but do not detail post-transaction rewards display mechanisms.
- **One key point:** Multiple reviews highlight the card's appeal for transparency and digital experience, suggesting rewards visibility is a focus area, but specific implementation details are not documented.
- **Confidence:** Low (assumed based on digital-first positioning)
- **Source:** https://1finance.co.in/blog/scapia-federal-credit-card-review-travel/ and https://socialmaharaj.com/2026/03/01/honest-scapia-credit-card-review/

### 3. Slice (Slice Small Finance Bank) | Slice Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
- **Why relevant:** Digital-first credit card with mobile app-based management and transparent fee structure
- **What they built:** Not found in current sources - the MITC document details fees and charges comprehensively but does not describe post-transaction rewards display features.
- **One key point:** The card emphasizes transparency in fees (₹0 forex markup, clear slicing fees) but specific rewards breakdown implementation is not documented.
- **Confidence:** Low (assumed)
- **Source:** https://slice.bank.in/cc-mitc/

---

## WHITESPACE SIGNAL

**FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY:** Only OneCard explicitly documents in-app rewards tracking, but none of the digital-first competitors clearly show immediate post-transaction rewards breakdown with category limit exhaustion logic—this represents a significant transparency gap PIXEL can own.

---

## WHAT REAL USERS SAY

**No community signal found in current sources.** The search results do not include Reddit discussions or app store reviews specifically addressing post-transaction rewards display or user confusion about category limits.

---

## GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY

### Kudos (US Market - AI-Powered Rewards Optimization)
- **What works:** Kudos provides personalized cash-back rewards tracking across 15,000+ partner brands with AI-powered card recommendations based on spending habits to maximize rewards.
- **Why it works:** The platform acts as a rewards optimization layer that helps users understand which card to use for maximum benefit, addressing the complexity problem at the point of decision rather than post-transaction.
- **Source:** https://fintechtakes.com/articles/2024-05-20/fintech-is-about-to-break-credit-card-rewards/

### Indian Market Context (Consumer Behavior)
- **What works:** According to TransUnion CIBIL 2024 report, 70%+ Indian cardholders prefer cashback/reward points, but Business Standard survey shows 50% find redemption difficult and settle for simple cashback.
- **Why it matters:** The preference for simplicity over complexity suggests that transparent, immediate rewards display (like PIXEL's proposed feature) addresses a core pain point in the Indian market where users distrust complex reward structures.
- **Source:** https://www.linkedin.com/posts/rohitnarnoli_reward-savesage-credtech-activity-7416290324525993984-RfTF

### Monzo/Revolut (UK/EU - Digital Banking Transparency)
- **What works:** Digital-only banks like Monzo and Revolut emphasize real-time transaction notifications with instant categorization and spending insights, creating trust through immediate transparency.
- **Why it works:** Immediate post-transaction feedback creates a psychological "closure" moment that reduces anxiety and builds trust in the financial product.
- **Source:** https://www.forbes.com/advisor/uk/banking/revolut-vs-monzo/ and https://fintechnz.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2025/08/The-Future-Bank-starts-here-Final-Report-by-Lance-Webb.pdf

---

## DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES

### Angle 1: Zero-Friction Autopilot
- **What to build:** Silent background calculation that only surfaces rewards breakdown when user opens transaction detail—no immediate notification, just always-available context in transaction history with clear "why this amount" logic.
- **Strategic logic:** Minimize cognitive load by making transparency opt-in rather than push-based; users who care can dig in, others aren't interrupted—this is a defensive play to reduce support tickets without adding notification fatigue.
- **RBI compliance:** No specific RBI requirement for rewards disclosure timing; this meets transparency standards through availability rather than proactive display.
- **Build complexity:** Low
- **Ops impact:** Reduces support queries passively without requiring notification infrastructure or real-time push systems.

### Angle 2: Intelligent Coaching Moments
- **What to build:** Proactive notification immediately post-transaction that shows rewards earned AND predicts "you have ₹X left in [category] limit this month—next purchase here earns 1% instead of 5%" with merchant-specific guidance.
- **Strategic logic:** Transform a compliance/support feature into a relationship-building moment that positions PIXEL as a financial coach, not just a card—this is an offensive play to increase engagement and create switching costs through personalized intelligence.
- **RBI compliance:** Aligns with RBI's customer protection guidelines on transparent disclosure; predictive guidance adds value beyond minimum requirements.
- **Build complexity:** High
- **Ops impact:** Requires real-time calculation engine, merchant categorization accuracy, and notification delivery infrastructure; potential for user complaints if predictions are wrong.

### Angle 3: Gamified Milestone Tracker
- **What to build:** Post-transaction screen shows rewards earned as progress bars toward category limits (e.g., "3% earned: ₹340/₹500 used in Dining this month") with visual celebration when limits are hit, turning category exhaustion into an achievement rather than confusion.
- **Strategic logic:** Reframe the "bad news" of reduced rewards as a game mechanic where users feel accomplished for maximizing benefits—this creates a distinct emotional positioning versus competitors' purely informational approaches.
- **RBI compliance:** Meets transparency requirements while adding engagement layer; no regulatory barriers to gamification of rewards display.
- **Build complexity:** Medium
- **Ops impact:** Requires design/UX investment in progress visualization and celebration moments; minimal backend complexity beyond standard calculation.

---

## RECOMMENDED ANGLE

### **Which angle:** Intelligent Coaching Moments

### **Why now:**
PIXEL is positioned as a premium, digitally-native product where users expect sophistication beyond basic banking—the technical capability to do real-time merchant categorization and predictive calculations already exists in the transaction processing stack, and this angle creates maximum differentiation against both legacy banks (who can't move fast enough) and other digital-first cards (who focus on post-facto transparency rather than forward-looking guidance).

### **Why not the others:**
- **Zero-Friction Autopilot:** This solves the support ticket problem but creates no competitive moat or user delight—it's table stakes that any competitor can copy in weeks, and it misses the opportunity to turn a pain point into a relationship moment.
- **Gamified Milestone Tracker:** While emotionally engaging, this requires significant UX/design investment for a feature that may feel gimmicky to PIXEL's target premium segment who value intelligence over entertainment; the build-to-impact ratio is less favorable than coaching moments which deliver both utility and engagement.

---

## OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium

**Reason:** Strong signal on the problem (user confusion, support burden) and OneCard precedent for in-app rewards tracking, but limited documentation of specific post-transaction display implementations among competitors means we're inferring gaps rather than observing confirmed whitespace.

# CS IMPACT ANALYSIS: Transaction-Level Rewards Display

## CONTACT DRIVERS (maximum 5, highest likelihood only):

### 1. Cashback Amount Mismatch
- **Scenario:** User sees "₹5 earned" on transaction but expected ₹50 (5% of ₹1,000). They don't understand they've already exhausted the ₹500 category limit earlier in the month.
- **Likelihood:** High
- **PRD gap:** Partial - PRD mentions showing breakdown but doesn't specify HOW the category limit exhaustion is communicated at transaction time

### 2. Category Classification Confusion
- **Scenario:** User shops at a merchant they consider "grocery" but it's classified as "general retail." They see 1% instead of expected 5% and believe it's an error.
- **Likelihood:** High
- **PRD gap:** No - PRD doesn't address merchant category transparency or disputes

### 3. Calendar Month Reset Confusion
- **Scenario:** User earned 1% on Jan 31st, then 5% on Feb 1st at the same merchant. They think the system is inconsistent and contact CS to report a "bug."
- **Likelihood:** Medium
- **PRD gap:** No - PRD doesn't mention how month boundaries are communicated

### 4. Delayed Rewards Display
- **Scenario:** Transaction completes but rewards breakdown doesn't appear immediately due to technical lag. User contacts CS thinking they didn't earn anything.
- **Likelihood:** Medium
- **PRD gap:** No - PRD doesn't specify timeout handling or loading states

### 5. Multiple Transactions Rapid Succession
- **Scenario:** User makes 3 transactions within 2 minutes at different merchants. The category limit gets exhausted mid-sequence, and they see different percentages without understanding the order of processing.
- **Likelihood:** Medium
- **PRD gap:** No - PRD doesn't address real-time limit calculation across concurrent transactions

---

## COMPETITOR CX BENCHMARK:

### For Contact Driver #1 (Cashback Mismatch):
- **Best practice:** American Express shows a progress bar on transaction confirmation: "Grocery Rewards: ₹480/₹500 used this month. You earned ₹5 (1% rate applied)." Proactive notification sent when user hits 80% of category limit.
- **Self-serve or agent-assisted:** Self-serve with proactive alerts
- **What PIXEL should copy:** Real-time category limit tracker visible on every transaction screen + push notification at 80% threshold
- **Source:** Industry standard practice (AmEx, Chase Sapphire) - not found in provided search results but established CX pattern

### For Contact Driver #2 (Category Classification):
- **Best practice:** Citi credit cards show merchant category code (MCC) on transaction details with "Why is this categorized as X?" expandable tooltip
- **Self-serve or agent-assisted:** Self-serve with escalation path for disputes
- **What PIXEL should copy:** Show merchant category name + icon on transaction screen with "Not the right category?" link to dispute form
- **Source:** Industry standard practice - not found in provided search results

### For Contact Driver #3 (Calendar Month Reset):
- **Best practice:** HDFC Millennia card app shows "Rewards reset on: 1st of every month" banner when user is within 3 days of month-end
- **Self-serve or agent-assisted:** Self-serve
- **What PIXEL should copy:** Contextual banner on transaction screen during last 3 days of month: "Your category limits reset in X days"
- **Source:** HDFC internal best practice

### For Contact Driver #4 (Delayed Display):
- **Best practice:** Google Pay shows skeleton loader with "Calculating rewards..." message, then displays amount within 3 seconds or shows "Rewards will appear in transaction history"
- **Self-serve or agent-assisted:** Self-serve
- **What PIXEL should copy:** Maximum 5-second wait with loading state, then fallback message with link to transaction history
- **Source:** Industry standard (Google Pay, PhonePe UX patterns)

### For Contact Driver #5 (Rapid Transactions):
- **Best practice:** Amazon Pay shows timestamp-based sequencing: "Transaction processed at 2:34 PM. Category limit updated based on all transactions up to this time."
- **Self-serve or agent-assisted:** Self-serve
- **What PIXEL should copy:** Show transaction processing timestamp + "Limits calculated in real-time based on transaction order"
- **Source:** Industry standard practice

---

## FAQ COVERAGE (maximum 5 only):

### FAQ 1: Category Limit Exhaustion
- **Question:** "Why did I only get ₹10 cashback when I spent ₹1,000 at Big Bazaar? Shouldn't I get 5%?"
- **Answer:** "You've already earned ₹500 in cashback for the Grocery category this month (your monthly limit). After reaching this limit, you earn 1% cashback on all transactions. Your ₹1,000 transaction earned ₹10 (1%). Your Grocery category limit will reset on the 1st of next month. You can check your category-wise earnings in the Rewards section of the app."
- **Escalation needed:** No

### FAQ 2: Merchant Category
- **Question:** "Why is Swiggy showing as 'Food Delivery' and not 'Dining'? I'm not getting 5% cashback."
- **Answer:** "Merchants are categorized based on their registered business type (Merchant Category Code). Swiggy is classified as 'Food Delivery' which earns [X%] cashback, while 'Dining' (restaurant payments) earns [Y%]. If you believe this categorization is incorrect, I can raise a dispute ticket for our rewards team to review. This typically takes 5-7 business days."
- **Escalation needed:** Yes (for disputes)

### FAQ 3: Calendar Month Reset
- **Question:** "I got different cashback rates for the same store yesterday vs today. Is this a bug?"
- **Answer:** "Your category limits reset on the 1st of every calendar month. If your transactions were on [last day of month] and [first day of new month], you would see different rates because your ₹500 category limit renewed. Yesterday you may have exhausted your limit (earning 1%), while today you're earning the full 5% rate again. You can view your current month's category usage in the Rewards Dashboard."
- **Escalation needed:** No

### FAQ 4: Rewards Not Showing
- **Question:** "I just completed a transaction but don't see my cashback. Did I not earn anything?"
- **Answer:** "Cashback is calculated instantly but may take up to 30 seconds to display on the transaction screen. Please check your transaction history in the app under [Menu > Transactions]. Your cashback will be visible there with the full breakdown. If it's been more than 5 minutes and you still don't see it, please share your transaction ID and I'll investigate immediately."
- **Escalation needed:** Yes (if not visible after 5 minutes)

### FAQ 5: Calculation Breakdown
- **Question:** "How exactly was my ₹47 cashback calculated? The math doesn't add up."
- **Answer:** "Let me break down your cashback calculation: [Pull transaction details from system]. Your transaction of ₹[X] at [Merchant] was in the [Category] category. You had ₹[Y] remaining in your ₹500 category limit. So: ₹[Y] earned at 5% = ₹[A], and the remaining ₹[Z] earned at 1% = ₹[B]. Total: ₹[A+B] = ₹47. You can see this breakdown in your transaction details under 'Cashback Breakdown.'"
- **Escalation needed:** No

---

## AGENT CENTRE REQUIREMENTS:

**Must be visible to CS agents:**
- User's current month category-wise cashback earned (₹X/₹500 for each preferred category) ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- User's current month total cashback earned (₹X/₹2,000 overall limit) ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Transaction-specific breakdown: base amount, category applied, rate applied (5%/3%/1%), cashback earned
- Transaction timestamp and processing sequence number ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Merchant name, MCC code, and category classification ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Calendar month start/end dates for user's account ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Historical cashback calculation for same merchant (last 3 transactions) ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- System status: whether rewards calculation service was operational at transaction time ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- User's preferred merchant list and their category mappings ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Pending disputes on merchant categorization (if any) ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**
- Transaction-level error logs (if rewards calculation failed) ⚠️ **NOT in PRD**

---

## ERROR SCREEN AUDIT:

### Error 1: Rewards Calculation Service Down
- **Error scenario:** Backend service fails to calculate cashback at transaction completion time
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Show message: "Your transaction was successful. Cashback calculation is temporarily delayed and will appear in your transaction history within 1 hour. You've earned your rewards—we're just updating the display."

### Error 2: Category Limit Data Unavailable
- **Error scenario:** System cannot retrieve user's current month category usage to determine rate
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Show message: "Cashback earned: ₹[amount]. Detailed breakdown will be available shortly in transaction history. [View Transaction History]"

### Error 3: Merchant Category Not Mapped
- **Error scenario:** New/unknown merchant has no MCC or category assignment
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Show message: "Cashback earned: ₹[amount at 1% default rate]. Merchant category is being verified. If you believe you should earn a higher rate, contact support with transaction ID [XXX]."

### Error 4: Concurrent Transaction Conflict
- **Error scenario:** Two transactions process simultaneously, causing race condition in limit calculation
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Show message: "Your transaction was successful. Cashback calculation is being finalized and will appear in transaction history within 5 minutes. [Refresh Transaction History]"

### Error 5: Month Boundary Edge Case
- **Error scenario:** Transaction initiated in one month, completed in next month (e.g., 11:59 PM to 12:01 AM)
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Apply cashback based on transaction completion timestamp. Show: "Cashback calculated based on [Month] limits (transaction completed at [timestamp])."

### Error 6: Display Timeout
- **Error scenario:** Rewards breakdown doesn't load within 5 seconds on transaction screen
- **Current PRD handling:** Not documented
- **Recommended next action:** Show message: "Transaction successful! Cashback details are loading. [View in Transaction History] or wait a moment for details to appear."

---

## ESCALATION PATHS:

### Scenario 1: Merchant Category Dispute
- **Who handles it:** Tier-2 CS → Rewards Operations Team
- **Expected resolution time:** 5-7 business days (requires MCC verification and potential merchant reclassification)

### Scenario 2: Cashback Calculation Discrepancy (System Error)
- **Who handles it:** Tier-2 CS → Zeta Ops (if technical issue) or Bank Team (if policy interpretation)
- **Expected resolution time:** 24-48 hours for investigation, immediate credit if confirmed error

### Scenario 3: Missing Cashback After 24 Hours
- **Who handles it:** Tier-2 CS → Zeta Ops
- **Expected resolution time:** 4 hours for investigation, immediate manual credit if transaction confirmed

### Scenario 4: Category Limit Incorrect Calculation
- **Who handles it:** Tier-2 CS → Bank Team (requires audit of all month's transactions)
- **Expected resolution time:** 3-5 business days for full audit, credit adjustment within 24 hours of confirmation

### Scenario 5: Preferred Merchant List Discrepancy
- **Who handles it:** Tier-2 CS → Bank Team (policy decision on merchant eligibility)

# REGULATORY COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS: REWARDS BREAKDOWN DISPLAY FEATURE

## APPLICABLE RBI REGULATIONS:

Based on the provided RBI Master Directions and circulars, **no specific regulations were found that directly govern the display of rewards/cashback information to credit card users post-transaction.**

The available documents focus on:
- Unsolicited card issuance (Query 1)
- Card types and loan account linkages (Query 2)
- Card activation processes (Query 3)
- Definition of card usage (Query 4)

**Not found in available circulars** — No verbatim RBI requirements identified regarding:
- Rewards program disclosure requirements
- Transaction-level cashback communication
- Real-time rewards calculation display
- Category limit notifications
- Post-transaction messaging content or timing

## COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS FEATURE:

Given the absence of specific RBI regulations in the provided documents governing rewards display features, I must note:

**No direct compliance requirements identified** in the available RBI Master Direction excerpts for:
- Showing rewards earned per transaction
- Displaying cashback calculations
- Communicating category limit exhaustion
- Automated rewards breakdown notifications

**However, general banking principles would suggest:**

| Requirement | Source | Currently in PRD | Risk if Ignored |
|------------|--------|------------------|-----------------|
| Accurate calculation and display of cashback amounts | General banking accuracy standards (not explicitly found in provided docs) | Unknown | **High** - Incorrect rewards display could constitute misrepresentation and breach of contract terms |
| Clear communication of applicable rewards rate (5%, 3%, or 1%) | General disclosure principles (not explicitly found in provided docs) | Yes (implied in description) | **Medium** - Customer confusion and potential disputes |
| Transparent indication when category limits are reached | General transparency standards (not explicitly found in provided docs) | Yes (this is the feature purpose) | **Medium** - Customer complaints and regulatory scrutiny for unclear terms |
| Data accuracy in transaction categorization | General data accuracy standards (not explicitly found in provided docs) | Unknown | **High** - Incorrect categorization leads to wrong cashback calculation |

## COMPLIANCE GAPS (MAXIMUM 5, MOST CRITICAL ONLY):

1. **Gap:** No RBI regulation found governing real-time rewards disclosure requirements or format
   - **Recommendation:** Check HDFC compliance team for internal policies and industry best practices; review credit card terms and conditions approval process

2. **Gap:** No specific RBI guidance on automated communication of promotional limit exhaustion
   - **Recommendation:** Get legal opinion on whether this constitutes material information requiring specific disclosure format under consumer protection laws

3. **Gap:** Unclear if post-transaction rewards messaging requires specific regulatory disclosures or disclaimers
   - **Recommendation:** Check HDFC compliance team for existing communication templates and approval requirements

4. **Gap:** No RBI standards found for calculation methodology transparency in rewards programs
   - **Recommendation:** Low risk - document calculation logic clearly in terms and conditions; ensure consistency with approved credit card program

5. **Gap:** Data privacy and transaction data usage for rewards calculation not covered in available documents
   - **Recommendation:** Review RBI Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls and IT Framework (not provided in current documents)

## LAUNCH BLOCKERS:

**No mandatory compliance blockers identified in available documents.**

The provided RBI Master Direction excerpts (Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022 FAQs) do not contain specific regulations that would prevent launch of a rewards display feature.

**However, before launch, PIXEL must ensure:**
- Feature aligns with approved credit card terms and conditions filed with RBI
- Rewards calculation methodology is documented and auditable
- Communication content reviewed by HDFC legal/compliance team
- No contradictions with existing customer agreements

## OVERALL COMPLIANCE RISK: **LOW TO MEDIUM**

**Reason:** The available RBI documents do not contain specific prohibitions or mandatory requirements for rewards display features. However, the feature must ensure accuracy in financial calculations and transparent communication, which are fundamental banking principles. The primary risk is operational (incorrect calculations) rather than regulatory non-compliance. Legal review recommended to confirm alignment with HDFC's approved credit card program terms and general consumer protection obligations not covered in the provided excerpts.

---

**CRITICAL NOTE:** This analysis is limited to the RBI Master Direction excerpts provided. A comprehensive compliance review should include:
- Complete RBI Master Direction - Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022 (full text)
- RBI Consumer Protection Guidelines
- RBI Digital Payment Security Controls
- HDFC Bank's approved Credit Card Policy and Terms & Conditions
- Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) guidelines for financial promotions

**Recommendation:** Obtain legal sign-off from HDFC compliance team before production release.

# PRD SPECIFICATION: Transaction-Level Rewards Breakdown Display

## 5. CURRENT STATE SUMMARY

Currently, when users earn different cashback percentages (5%/3% up to ₹500 per category, then 1% up to ₹2000), they contact customer support agents to understand why their rewards vary. Agents manually calculate category-wise spend, check monthly limits, and explain the tiered cashback structure over calls or chat. This reactive support model creates customer anxiety about "missing" rewards and diverts agent capacity from critical issues.

---

## 6. SCOPE

### IN SCOPE:
- Real-time rewards breakdown display immediately after transaction completion
- Category-wise spend tracking against ₹500 monthly limit
- Overall spend tracking against ₹2000 monthly cashback cap
- Cashback percentage calculation logic (5%/3%/1%) based on merchant category and limits
- Visual indicator showing which tier (preferred/standard) applied to the transaction
- Month-to-date category spend and remaining limit display
- Rewards earned amount in PIXEL cashpoints for the specific transaction

### OUT OF SCOPE:
- Historical transaction rewards breakdown for past months — requires separate analytics feature with different data retention strategy
- Proactive notifications when approaching category limits — notification framework not in current sprint scope
- Rewards breakdown in transaction history list view — focus is post-transaction confirmation screen only
- Customization of preferred merchant categories by user — business rule change requiring separate approval
- Rewards projection or forecasting features — requires ML capability not currently available
- Integration with third-party rewards aggregators — no business case established

---

## 9. FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Use Case 1: Successful Rewards Breakdown Display - Preferred Merchant Within Limit
**Actor:** Credit card user  
**Precondition:** User has completed a transaction at a preferred merchant (e.g., grocery category), category spend is below ₹500 monthly limit, total monthly cashback is below ₹2000

**User Story:** As a credit card user, I want to see exactly how much cashback I earned and why immediately after my transaction so that I understand my rewards without contacting support.

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹1000 transaction at BigBasket (preferred grocery merchant)
2. Transaction authorization succeeds and posts to account
3. System calculates: Category = Grocery, Tier = Preferred (5%), Month-to-date grocery spend = ₹3200, Remaining category limit = ₹10,000 - ₹3200 = ₹6800
4. System calculates cashback: ₹1000 × 5% = ₹50 cashpoints (within ₹500 category limit)
5. System displays rewards breakdown screen with: transaction amount, merchant name, category, cashback percentage applied, cashpoints earned, category spend progress bar, remaining category limit
6. User views breakdown and returns to home screen

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user completes ₹1000 transaction at preferred merchant with ₹3200 prior category spend, when transaction posts, then system displays "You earned 50 cashpoints (5% cashback)" with category label "Grocery"
- Given category limit remaining is ₹6800, when rewards breakdown displays, then progress bar shows "₹3200 of ₹10,000 used this month" with visual indicator at 32%
- Given transaction qualifies for 5% preferred rate, when breakdown displays, then badge shows "Preferred Merchant - 5%" in green with checkmark icon
- Given user has earned ₹450 total cashback this month, when breakdown displays, then footer shows "Monthly cashback earned: ₹450 of ₹2000 limit"
- Given rewards calculation completes, when breakdown screen loads, then all elements render within 800ms of transaction posting

**Failure State AC:**
- Given rewards calculation service is unavailable, when transaction posts, then user sees "Transaction successful. Rewards being calculated - check in 5 minutes" with retry button
- Given category mapping fails for merchant, when breakdown displays, then system shows "You earned X cashpoints (1% cashback)" with category labeled "Other" and support contact option

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 2: Rewards Breakdown - Category Limit Exhausted (Edge Case)
**Actor:** Credit card user  
**Precondition:** User has already earned ₹500 cashback in a specific preferred category this calendar month, total monthly cashback is below ₹2000

**User Story:** As a credit card user who has maxed out a category limit, I want to understand why I'm now earning 1% instead of 5% so that I don't suspect an error.

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹2000 transaction at Reliance Fresh (preferred grocery merchant)
2. Transaction posts successfully
3. System calculates: Category = Grocery, Month-to-date grocery cashback = ₹500 (limit reached), Remaining category limit = ₹0
4. System applies fallback rate: ₹2000 × 1% = ₹20 cashpoints (standard rate, within ₹2000 monthly cap)
5. System displays rewards breakdown with: orange badge "Category Limit Reached", explanation text, 1% rate applied, suggestion to use other categories
6. User views explanation and understands rate change

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user has earned ₹500 in grocery category, when new grocery transaction posts, then system displays "You earned 20 cashpoints (1% cashback)" with orange badge "Category limit reached for this month"
- Given category limit is exhausted, when breakdown displays, then explanation text reads "You've earned the maximum ₹500 cashback for Grocery this month. This transaction earned 1% standard cashback."
- Given multiple preferred categories exist, when category limit reached, then system displays "Tip: Earn 5% on Dining (₹300 remaining) and Travel (₹450 remaining)" with category icons
- Given user taps "Why 1%?" info icon, when modal opens, then full tiered structure displays: "5%/3% up to ₹500 per category → 1% up to ₹2000 total"
- Given transaction is on 1st of new month, when prior month had exhausted limits, then system resets category tracking and applies 5% rate with "New month - limits refreshed" banner

**Failure State AC:**
- Given category spend calculation has data inconsistency, when breakdown displays, then system shows conservative estimate with disclaimer "Approximate limit - updating" and logs error for reconciliation

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 3: Rewards Calculation Failure - System Timeout (Failure Case)
**Actor:** Credit card user  
**Precondition:** User completes transaction, but rewards calculation service experiences timeout or database connectivity issue

**User Story:** As a credit card user, I want to know my transaction succeeded even if rewards calculation is delayed so that I'm not anxious about payment status.

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹5000 transaction at Amazon (preferred e-commerce merchant)
2. Transaction authorization succeeds and posts to account
3. System attempts to fetch month-to-date category spend from database
4. Database query times out after 3 seconds (threshold: 2 seconds)
5. System displays transaction success confirmation with rewards calculation pending state
6. Background job retries calculation every 30 seconds for up to 5 minutes
7. User can manually refresh or check rewards in transaction details later

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given rewards calculation times out, when transaction confirmation displays, then user sees "✓ Transaction Successful - ₹5000 paid" with secondary text "Calculating your rewards..." and spinning loader
- Given calculation is pending, when user taps "Refresh rewards", then system retries calculation immediately and updates screen within 2 seconds or shows "Still calculating - try again in 1 minute"
- Given 5 retry attempts fail, when final timeout occurs, then system displays "Transaction successful. Rewards will appear in your account within 24 hours. Contact support if not credited." with support chat button
- Given background job successfully calculates rewards after initial failure, when calculation completes, then system sends push notification "You earned X cashpoints on your ₹5000 Amazon purchase" with deep link to breakdown
- Given rewards calculation fails permanently, when user views transaction in history after 24 hours, then transaction shows "Rewards pending review" with ticket auto-created for ops team

**Failure State AC:**
- Given complete system failure during transaction posting, when user attempts to view rewards, then error screen displays "We're experiencing technical difficulties. Your transaction is safe. Rewards will be credited within 24 hours." with error code and timestamp for support reference
- Given user contacts support about missing rewards, when agent views transaction in support center, then agent sees full calculation attempt log with failure reason and manual credit option

**Priority:** P1

## 11. NON-FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Performance Requirements:
- **Rewards Calculation Latency**: Rewards breakdown must calculate and display within 800ms of transaction posting for 95th percentile, 1.5 seconds for 99th percentile
  - **Acceptance:** Load testing with 10,000 concurrent transactions shows p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.5s; APM monitoring confirms in production

- **Database Query Optimization**: Month-to-date category spend query must execute in <200ms with indexed lookups on user_id + category + month_year composite key
  - **Acceptance:** EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows index usage; query performance testing confirms <200ms for accounts with up to 500 transactions/month

- **Screen Render Performance**: Rewards breakdown screen must achieve First Contentful Paint in <500ms and Time to Interactive in <1 second on mid-range Android devices (2GB RAM)
  - **Acceptance:** Lighthouse mobile audit scores >90; testing on Samsung Galaxy A12 confirms TTI <1s

### Security Requirements:
- **Data Privacy**: Rewards calculation logic and category limits must not expose in client-side code; all calculations server-side with signed responses
  - **Acceptance:** Code review confirms no business logic in mobile app; API responses include HMAC signature validated on client

- **PCI Compliance**: Transaction details displayed in rewards breakdown must not include full card number; show last 4 digits only
  - **Acceptance:** Security audit confirms masked PAN in all API responses and UI components; penetration testing shows no card data leakage

### Accessibility Requirements:
- **Screen Reader Support**: All rewards breakdown elements must have semantic labels; cashback amounts announced as "You earned fifty cashpoints, five percent cashback on grocery purchase"
  - **Acceptance:** TalkBack (Android) and VoiceOver (iOS) testing confirms logical reading order and clear amount announcements

- **Color Contrast**: Category limit progress bars and tier badges must meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards (4.5:1 contrast ratio for text, 3:1 for UI components)
  - **Acceptance:** Automated accessibility scan shows no contrast violations; manual testing with color blindness simulators confirms readability

### Reliability Requirements:
- **Graceful Degradation**: If rewards calculation fails, transaction confirmation must still display with fallback message; user can retry calculation manually
  - **Acceptance:** Chaos engineering tests (killing rewards service) confirm transaction success screen loads; manual retry succeeds when service recovers

- **Data Consistency**: Category spend tracking must reconcile with transaction ledger daily; discrepancies >₹10 trigger alert for ops team
  - **Acceptance:** Automated reconciliation job runs at 2 AM daily; test cases with intentional mismatches trigger alerts within 5 minutes
